categories.main_business_segments: IDACORP is a holding company whose principal operating subsidiary is Idaho Power, an electric utility engaged in the generation, transmission, distribution, sale, and purchase of electric energy and capacity. Idaho Power serves approximately 633,000 retail customers in southern Idaho and eastern Oregon. IDACORP's other notable subsidiaries include IDACORP Financial Services, Inc., which invests in affordable housing and real estate tax credit projects, and Ida-West Energy Company, which operates small hydropower generation projects.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Idaho Power operates 17 hydropower projects on the Snake River and its tributaries with 1,818 MW capacity, co-owns two coal-fired plants (Jim Bridger in Wyoming with one-third interest and North Valmy in Nevada with 50 percent interest), and operates three natural gas-fired plants in Idaho. The company also utilizes battery storage (131 MW installed as of 2023, with plans for 304 MW by end of 2025) and participates in the Western Energy Imbalance Market for efficient dispatch of generation resources.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Idaho Power serves approximately 532,000 residential customers and principal commercial and industrial customers involved in food processing, electronics, general manufacturing, agriculture, health care, government, and education. The company also serves irrigation customers who use electricity to operate irrigation pumps during the agricultural growing season. Approximately 95 percent of retail revenue originates from Idaho-located customers, with the remainder from Oregon.
categories.geographic_coverage: Idaho Power operates exclusively in southern Idaho and eastern Oregon, covering approximately 24,000 square miles with an estimated population of 1.4 million. The company holds franchises in 72 cities in Idaho and 7 cities in Oregon, and holds certificates to serve all or a portion of 25 counties in Idaho and 3 counties in Oregon. All IDACORP and Idaho Power employees work in the United States.
categories.supply_chain_position: Idaho Power operates as a vertically integrated utility, controlling generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity. The company is positioned midstream to downstream in the energy supply chain, generating power from its own facilities and purchasing additional power through long-term contracts and wholesale markets to serve retail customers. Idaho Power also sells excess generation and transmission services in wholesale markets.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: IDACORP's strategy focuses on four areas: keeping employees safe and engaged, growing financial strength, improving Idaho Power's core business, and enhancing Idaho Power's brand. Key initiatives include achieving 100 percent clean energy by 2045, reducing carbon emissions intensity by 35 percent for 2021-2025 and 86 percent by 2030 (compared to 2005 baseline), converting coal-fired units to natural gas, integrating renewable resources (solar, wind, geothermal), developing battery storage and hydrogen generation capabilities, and constructing transmission infrastructure including the Boardman-to-Hemingway and Gateway West projects.
categories.revenue_model: Idaho Power generates revenue primarily through the sale of electricity to retail customers (residential, commercial, industrial, and irrigation segments), wholesale energy sales, transmission wheeling services, and energy efficiency program revenues. Retail rates are determined on a cost-of-service basis through regulatory proceedings, with mechanisms including power cost adjustment mechanisms, a fixed cost adjustment mechanism in Idaho, and tariff riders for cost recovery.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Idaho Power's electric utility business is recognized as a natural monopoly within its service territory, with no direct competitors for retail electric service. However, the company competes with natural gas providers for customer energy needs and faces competition from customer-owned solar and distributed generation. Idaho Power participates in wholesale energy markets and transmission markets regulated by FERC, where it competes with other utilities and energy providers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: IDACORP achieved net income of $261.2 million in 2023, with total electric utility operating revenues of $1,762.9 million. The company has achieved net income growth for sixteen consecutive years. Idaho Power's customer count grew 2.4 percent in 2023, and the company's MWh sales to retail customers in 2023 were the second highest in its history. IDACORP's market capitalization was approximately $5.2 billion as of June 30, 2023.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Idaho Power emphasizes reliable, affordable, clean energy delivery with a focus on operational excellence and safety. The company differentiates through its diversified generation portfolio (55 percent hydropower, 21 percent coal, 24 percent natural gas in 2023), significant renewable energy integration plans, battery storage investments, and commitment to carbon emissions reduction. Idaho Power provides uninterrupted service 99.97 percent of the time and ranks in the top 30 percent of U.S. utilities in safety performance, while maintaining competitive rates through efficient operations and regulatory mechanisms.
